answer: On a dry mesa terrace, a walnut nursery rents one numbered bed to each agent for one grafted sapling, judged over a three-year horizon. The keeper waters it through three dry seasons while a neighboring keeper inspects the graft union each spring and records whether the bud took. A failed graft or a missed spring check empties the bed for a year, and only beds with three straight passed checks earn a trading slot. A thousand fake keepers need a thousand grafted saplings and a thousand springs of neighbor checks, while one honest keeper pays it once.
